payload.title: How to Choose a Wedding Planner in Italy
payload.title_note: User's title kept: it is clear and contains the keyword variant 'wedding planner in Italy'. Suggested SEO title (under 60 characters): 'Wedding Planner Italy: How to Choose One from Australia'. H1 stays as the user's title.
secondary_keywords: how to choose a wedding planner in italy
questions to ask an italy wedding planner

audience.notes: Sophie and Marcus: Sydney professionals in their 30s, AUD 150K to 250K, 70 to 110 guests, Italy in 12 to 18 months, well travelled but have never organised anything in Italy. They do not know how Italian planners charge, what full planning vs coordination includes, or how to check references. Margaret (paying parent) reads every line for money handling, legal validity, who is on the ground and how older guests are looked after. Kayla (anti-persona) should feel this is not for her: no 'cheap' framing, no discount talk, no 'skip the planner fee' hacks.

payload.search_intent: Commercial investigation. Searchers are shortlisting Italian planners; Google serves planner homepages, directories and forum threads. We answer the question underneath the search (how do we pick the right one, and can we trust them?) so the page earns the informational slot and the 'how to choose' long tail.
payload.angle: The Australian couple's guide to choosing and checking an Italian wedding planner: decide which kind of help your wedding needs, understand how Italian planners charge and who they work for, ask the questions that separate a reliable planner from a polished Instagram feed, and know how it works from Australia. Wedded Wonderland Concierge appears honestly as an independent advisory and matchmaking layer that may recommend a partnered planner or help you move forward without one; it is never presented as the planner.
serp_gaps_to_win: Fee models explained plainly (flat fee, percentage, minimum fee, supplier commissions or mark-ups) and how to get them disclosed in writing. Ranking pages hide fees or quote packages without scope.
Planning from Australia: time difference, meeting rhythm, whether to visit, who is physically on site on the day. No ranking page is written for Australians.
How to judge a planner's answers, not just which questions to ask (good answer vs warning sign).
The honest service ladder: venue in-house coordinator, on-the-day coordinator, partial planner, full planner, designer, and an advisory or matchmaking layer, with when each is enough.
Regional specialist vs nationwide agency vs Australia-and-Italy planner, and why it matters for Lake Como vs Puglia vs Tuscany.
Money and paperwork for the payer: deposits in EUR, who pays suppliers, contract language, cancellation terms, currency risk.
The invisible work to confirm they handle: guest transfers, wet weather and heat plans, older guests, room blocks, legal or symbolic ceremony.
A trustworthy alternative to crowdsourcing planners in Facebook groups and Reddit, which rank in most markets.

outline.h2: First, decide what kind of help your wedding needs
outline.answers: Do we need a full planner, or would a venue coordinator, a partial planner or an adviser be enough?
must_include: The service ladder in a short comparison list or table: venue in-house coordinator, on-the-day coordinator, partial planning, full planning, design-led studio, advisory or matchmaking (what each does and does not cover)
Where the venue coordinator stops (usually at the venue's own gates: not guest transfers, other events or outside suppliers); researcher to source
Honest line that not every wedding needs a full planner (from the live concierge page), e.g. a small wedding at a hotel with strong in-house events
A 70 to 110 guest, multi-day wedding with guests flying from Australia is usually full-planning territory; say why without promising
Link to /expert-advice/do-you-really-need-a-wedding-planner-for-a-destination-wedding instead of re-arguing the whole question

outline.h2: Italian, Australian or both: where your planner should be based
outline.answers: Should we hire a planner in Italy, one based in Australia who works in Italy, or a mix?
must_include: Trade-offs: Italy-based (on-the-ground supplier relationships, language, site visits) vs Australia-based or dual-based (same time zone for calls, Australian contracts and expectations) vs both
Regional specialist vs nationwide agency: Lake Como, Amalfi, Tuscany and Puglia run on different supplier networks and logistics; ask where they have actually worked
Time difference between Sydney and Italy and how good planners handle it (scheduled calls, shared planning documents, response-time commitments). Researcher to confirm hours for AEST/AEDT vs CET/CEST
Ask who will be physically on site on the day and whether that is the person you have been planning with
Link the destination pages for Lake Como, Amalfi Coast and Tuscany where regions are named

outline.h2: How Italian wedding planners charge, and who they work for
outline.answers: How much will a planner cost, how is it calculated, and are they paid by suppliers too?
must_include: Fee models: flat fee for a written scope, percentage of the wedding budget, minimum fees; where the fee sits relative to the total. Every figure needs a dated source in EUR with an AUD approximation and conversion date, flagged for Nic

Supplier commissions and mark-ups: ask directly whether they receive commissions or rebates from venues or suppliers and ask for it in writing. Do not allege any planner does this; frame as a standard question
What the fee usually excludes (travel and accommodation for the planner team, site visits, extra events, overtime)
Link /expert-advice/cost-of-wedding-planner for full fee detail and /expert-advice/how-much-does-a-wedding-in-italy-cost for whole-budget context; do not duplicate their tables
No Concierge prices anywhere

outline.h2: The questions that separate a great planner from a great Instagram
outline.answers: What should we ask on the first call, and what does a good answer sound like?
must_include: A question list with 'a good answer sounds like' and 'a warning sign' for each (table or paired bullets). Cover: weddings per season and how many on the same weekend; who leads ours and attends the day; recent weddings at our venue or region in our month; references we can call, ideally a couple who planned from overseas; their Plan B at our venue; how they choose suppliers; how they quote and invoice; business registration and insurance (researcher to confirm what Italian businesses must hold, e.g. VAT number)
Ask to see a full wedding run sheet or a complete gallery, not a highlight reel
Link /how-to-choose-wedding-vendors-abroad for the general vetting method and /how-to-choose-the-right-destination-wedding-planner for the general checklist

outline.h2: The work you never see, and how to check they handle it
outline.answers: Beyond styling, what should a planner in Italy be doing for our guests and for us?
must_include: Invisible work: guest transfers between airport, hotels and venue; wet-weather and heat plans for outdoor ceremonies; older or less mobile guests (stairs, boats, cobblestones, walking distances); room blocks and guest accommodation; welcome and farewell events; local rules such as music licensing or noise limits (researcher to source, e.g. SIAE)

Legal: civil, religious or symbolic ceremony; whether the planner handles the Italian paperwork; that legal requirements must be confirmed for your own passports, with an official source (DFAT/Smartraveller or Italian consulate) checked within 12 months; link the Italy legal guide
No weather, availability or approval guarantees
Mid-article soft CTA here (one sentence)

outline.h2: Contracts, deposits and paying in euros from Australia
outline.answers: How do we protect the budget when contracts and payments are in another country and currency?
must_include: What a planner contract should state: scope, inclusions and exclusions, named lead planner, payment schedule, cancellation and postponement terms, what happens if the planner cannot attend
Whether you pay suppliers directly or through the planner, and why transparency matters either way
Contract language: ask for English or a translation of key terms

Currency: deposits and balances in EUR, exchange-rate movement over 12 to 18 months; a plain approach (track in one budget, know each due date). Link /wonderland-studio for multi-currency budget tracking
Brand fact allowed: the concierge coordinates 'deposits, payments and currency so nothing gets lost across borders' (from /wonderland-concierge)

outline.h2: Red flags to walk away from
outline.answers: What should make us stop and look elsewhere?
must_include: Vague or verbal-only fees; refusal to disclose commissions; pressure to book their suppliers only; no named on-day lead; promises about weather or 'guaranteed' dates; slow or inconsistent replies before you have even signed; no references from overseas couples; portfolio only from styled shoots
Keep it short: a list of 6 to 8 items

outline.answers: What does the concierge do, and how is it different from hiring a planner?
must_include: Exact positioning from the live page: an advisory and matchmaking service; 'Unlike a traditional wedding planner, we act as your trusted advisor and strategic partner during the sourcing and decision-making process. Depending on your wedding, we may recommend a partnered planner, or help you move forward confidently without one.'

Italian planners are partners; name a planner only via a confirmed on-site profile (e.g. /vendor/italian-style-weddings, /vendor/giritaly, both found by Firecrawl map on 22 Oct 2026), and only if the team confirms they suit the context
Use the process step names (Discovery Call, Destination and Venue Strategy, Planning Assessment, Vendor Curation, Concierge Support, Travel and Honeymoon Concierge), briefly
One proof point at most (e.g. 800+ weddings and celebrations, 54 countries)
No prices, no testimonials

must_include: Couple fear 1 (hiring the wrong planner: polished on Instagram but unreliable, overstretched or taking kickbacks): answered by the questions section, the fee and commissions section and red flags
Couple fear 2 (planning from the other side of the world: time zones, slow replies, no one on the ground): answered by the 'where your planner should be based' section and the on-site lead question
Paying parent fears (hidden costs and currency; legal validity): answered by the fees and contracts sections and an officially sourced legal line
At least one section showing the invisible work (H2 5)
Primary keyword in the H1 (as 'wedding planner in Italy'), in the first 100 words and in one H2 or the FAQ
Key takeaways (3 to 5 complete sentences)
Honest statement that not every wedding needs a full planner
Australian spelling; EUR figures with AUD approximation, source and conversion date
must_avoid: Naming or linking any planner without a confirmed /vendor/<slug> profile on our site; never link a planner's own website
Linking competitors or lead directories seen in the SERP (WeddingWire, Junebug, Hitched, The Knot, WedMeGood, Easy Weddings, The Anti-Bride, truewedstory) or Facebook and Reddit threads
Reusing competitor copy, headings or package prices (e.g. Amore Wedding Italy package figures, the AI Overview fee range attributed to a directory)
A 'best wedding planners in Italy' listicle format (our /italian-wedding-planners-luxury-wedding-italy page already does this)
Concierge prices; describing the Concierge as a wedding planner; placeholder or unapproved testimonials
Alleging that any named planner takes kickbacks
Banned words from the style guide, em dashes, and 'luxury' more than twice
Budget hacks aimed at the bargain hunter ('skip the planner fee', 'cheap', 'deals')
payload.word_count_rationale: The AU top 3 are a planner homepage (about 400 words), a Facebook thread and a directory (about 1,350): not comparable content. The ranking pages that serve the 'how to choose' intent run 800 (elleffevents), 3,500 (Italian Wedding Designer FAQ) and 3,800 (truewedstory, half of it a shortlist and photography advice); median 3,500. Target 2,400 to 3,000 so the piece is the most complete criteria-led guide without padding; fee detail and the legal process are delegated to existing pages by link.

cta.soft: If you would rather not vet planners yourself, your concierge can recommend one from our partnered network.

payload.differentiation: No existing page targets 'wedding planner italy' with a how-to-choose intent. This piece is Italy-specific and Australia-specific (time zones, AUD, legal recognition at home, paying from Australia), focused on the selection decision: which kind of planner, how they charge and whether they take commissions, how to judge their answers, and the invisible work to confirm. It links to the general planner checklist, the Italy planner list, the 'do you need a planner' piece and the planner-cost guide rather than repeating them, and uses descriptive anchors (never the exact keywords those pages own). Overlap is partial everywhere, so a new article is right. Recommendation for later (not this run): /how-to-choose-the-right-destination-wedding-planner is thin and dated (2023) and could be refreshed or consolidated once this piece is live.
